newsitem.title: USA: Deadly Empire State shooting seen as random attack.
newsitem.headline: Deadly Empire State shooting seen as random attack.

text.p: A deadly shooting spree by an elderly Palestinian who smuggled a semiautomatic handgun onto the observation deck of the Empire State Building was an apparently random attack and not a terrorist act, authorities said on Monday.

The gunman, identified as 69-year-old Palestinian Ali Abu Kamal, killed a young rock musician from Denmark and wounded six other people before taking his own life in Sunday's shooting, which prompted a review of security at one of New York's classic tourist spots.

"So far, there is no connection to a terrorist group, no other incident after that, no threat before," New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said on NBC's "Today" show. "It will have to be investigated but as it's being investigated, people shouldn't jump to that conclusion."
Law enforcement sources said the police investigation had tentatively concluded the shooting was a random act of violence, but they cautioned that the probe had yet to be completed.

Empire State Building owners were meeting on Monday to review security at the landmark, which does not have metal detectors like many buildings in New York City, from its most famous skyscrapers to high schools.
A building security camera tape was turned over to police, said Empire State building spokesman Howard Rubenstein. The tape shows the gunman on the way up to the observation deck.
"He was wearing a long coat. The gun was not visible and presumably it was hidden under his coat," Rubenstein said.

The gunman shot dead a Danish musician in his 20s and wounded six other people -- a Connecticut man who played in the same rock group, a 52-year-old Argentine man, a 30-year-old Swiss man, a 35-year old Bronx, N.Y. man and a married couple from Verdun, France.
Police said the gunman died without regaining consciousness in a New York hospital about six hours after he shot the tourists and then turned the gun on himself.
Three of the wounded were in critical condition on Monday and three others serious but stable, hospital officials said.
Several other people were injured in the pandemonium that broke out after the shooting on the 86th floor observation deck, which was crowded with tourists on a sunny Sunday afternoon.
The attack was the worst bloodshed at the 102-story building since July 1945, when a B-25 bomber lost in fog crashed into the 79th floor, killing 14 people and injuring 26 others.

Giuliani told a news conference on Sunday night that a joint terrorism task force of the Federal Bureau of Investigation and city police was investigating the shootings, even though it was not yet known whether the gunman was politically motivated.

Officials said the gunman was carrying documents from the Palestinian Authoritiy that showed he lived in Ramallah on the West Bank and was born in Jaffa. He came to New York in December and bought the .380-calibre Beretta used in the shooting in Florida at the end of January. Police said a receipt for the gun was found on his body.

The Empire State Building, which opened in 1931, is one of New York City's top tourist attractions, and at 1,250 feet (380 metres) high, it ranked for decades as the world's tallest building. In 1972, the Art Deco landmark was overtaken by the twin towers of the World Trade Centre.
